question.text: If <math><mi>m</mi></math> number of integers greater than <math><mn>7000</mn></math> can be formed with the digits <math><mn>3,5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7,8</mn></math> and <math><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo></math> such that no digit is being repeated, then the value of <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> is

solution.text:
A five digit integer is always greater than 7000.
The number of such integers are 5P5=5!=120.
For a four digit integer to be greater than 7000, it must begin with 7,8 or 9.
The number of such integers are 34P3=72.
Hence, the required number of such integers are 120+72=192.
⇒m=192
⇒m100=1.92.
